utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before the Defence calls its next witness, I would first like to go through the documents that have been tendered through witness, I think it was DP53. Yes, it was DP53, last Friday. Madam Registrar, could you please assist us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1795, under seal, pseudonym sheet; Exhibit D1796, map, sniping incident 3, marked by witness; Exhibit D1797, black and white photocopy of Prosecution Exhibit P3760, marked by witness; Exhibit D1798, black and white photocopy of Prosecution Exhibit P3758, marked by witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Since I hear no objections, they are all admitted into evidence. Number 1795, that is, Defence Exhibit, under seal. Then before calling the next witness, that would be DP -- and let me just find the right number -- I take it that would be DP23, Ms. Pilipovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We still have to decide on the protective measures. In the decision of the 19th of November it says that additional information was not yet provided. Meanwhile, it is, Mr. Ierace, I see a filing dated the 20th of November which provides additional information. Is there any observation the Prosecution would like to make then? The protective measures are granted as sought, that means facial distortion and pseudonym. Ms. Pilipovic, is the Defence ready to -- yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the next witness will be taken by Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The reason he is not present is that we were handed a letter just before you entered the courtroom indicating that there are an additional eight exhibits to come in through this witness. Mr. Stamp has left the Trial Chamber to obtain some further material in relation to those eight exhibits. I am happy for the examination-in-chief to start, provided that doesn't impact on the permissibility of Mr. Stamp's cross-examining the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if the Defence may respond. Does Mr. Ierace mean the letter dated the 24th of November in relation to Exhibit P3763, 3757, and 3762?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these are photographs that we received from the Prosecution for the first witness, so not in relation to the witness who was here on Friday, DP23, but the witness before him, that these photographs, if I may assist my colleague, these are not new exhibits. I just wanted to inform the Chamber and the Prosecution that we will also be showing these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that may be a little unintentionally misleading. They are not photographs that were shown to the last witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Ms. Pilipovic said not the last but the one that was before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, they weren't tendered through that witness, and there is a sketch as well which is including amongst them that relates to the photographs. And I think the photographs originally were tendered in the Prosecution case. I think that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In other words, there's a focus on the evidence of a particular Prosecution witness which is now apparent, and we wish to refresh our memory of the testimony of that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I think you mentioned three exhibits that were, well, let's say, reasonably shown to the Defence witness by the Prosecution. And you mentioned three numbers. But I see on your list, I see eight "P" numbers, and on the initial list, only one, so that would be seven new, minus three, remains four unexpected exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I owe you an explanation. In relation to photographs 3131, these are also Prosecution exhibits, and also the sketch P2424. So perhaps for my colleagues that will be something new. But if that is a problem, then the Defence will not show the photographs. Since P3131, that was tendered through a protected witness, and P3131 is a set of eight photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am not seeking to prevent the Defence to show photographs to witnesses, I am just trying to find out to what extent the late information as to the exhibits to be used would justify a -- the Prosecution to split up the cross-examination and to justify the absence of Mr. Stamp, who is supposed to do the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it will assist, I don't propose to split the cross-examination for that reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but I am not expressing myself properly, to justify that Mr. Stamp, although not present during the examination-in-chief would do the cross-examination. There he is. Sometimes time solves problems. Mr. Stamp, we discussed what to do with the cross-examination if you would not have been present during the examination-in-chief, but the problem has solved itself. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the reason of your temporary absence has been explained by Mr. Ierace. I think then we could start with the examination of the witness. Ms. Pilipovic, is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please assist us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. DP23, because that's how we will call you. Protective measures have been granted in your respect, that means that the outside world will not see your face and we will not use your name. Mr. DP23, before giving evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration of which the text will now be handed out to you by Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, please be seated, Mr. DP23. Ms. Pilipovic, where you made reference to the witness then DP23 before, I take it that you -- it was just a mistake and that you meant to refer to Witness DP53. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. DP23, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Before I start asking you questions I will show you a document so you can confirm whether the information contained in the document is correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, the information is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, would it be a suitable moment to go into closed session? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into closed session, but private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, if I may just use one opportunity during the private session. During the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are already in open session, Ms. Pilipovic. It goes so quick. But if you -- if there is any need to return in private session, please tell me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it doesn't have to be private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session now. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, I just wanted to warn you, when we are discussing some names during the examination, if you wish to give a name or someone's last name, if you don't want to say that in open session, could you please let me know so that we can go into closed session, considering that we are maybe speaking about some witnesses and some last names of people who may have appeared here as protected witnesses, and we do not wish to disclose their identity. Witness, thank you. Mr. DP23 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you just said is the more true since the LiveNote of the Registry is not functioning at this moment, so it will be difficult to make a redaction to the transcript. So may I ask both parties to be very cautious at this very moment. Please proceed

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, you told us that you lived in the settlement of Mrkovici in 1992 in September, and we will be speaking about the month of September 1992 until August 1994. Can you tell us whether in September 1992 you were engaged as a military person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I was engaged in the Company of Mrkovici in Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when was the Mrkovici Company established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: The Mrkovici Company was officially established when the Army of Republika Srpska was established, except that in a certain way, even before then we functioned. Because we self-organised ourselves because there were attacks from the opposing side, so in a kind of defence way, we were already organised and established.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You tell us that in your settlement you proceeded to self-organisation. Can you tell us whether you were armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, we were armed. To start with, not many -- we didn't have many weapons. We had some automatic rifles of the reserve police force. Later on, we managed to get weapons before the establishment of the Army of Republika Srpska. Sometime, I think it was in April in 1992. What happened then was that weapons were taken from the barracks of Faletici.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, were you armed, personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what weapons did you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I think you said "automatic rifles," in plural. I meant you personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, had I had an automatic rifles because I am a retired SUP officer. All police force members and they all had had issued automatic weapons to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that before September 1992 in the area where you were engaged and where your company was, there were attacks. Can you tell us who was taking part in these attacks? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. Before the conflict itself broke out there were barricades which had been erected in Sarajevo. To be more specific, a barricade had been erected in Sedrenik at the entrance to the Seven Woods, of the Sedam Suma, that was the only route that could be used to approach --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I am going to interrupt you. When you said you had been attacked, who attacked you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Muslims attacked us from Breka, Sedrenik, Budakovici, Hrastova, 1 and 2, et cetera. From these areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say they were Muslims from Breka, Sedrenik, Hrastovo. As good neighbours, did you discuss this matter and attempt to hold a meeting and to discuss this matter?, the engagement of your side, their side and the attacks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, we had discussions on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you said that you had discussions on several occasions, did you receive instructions for those meetings, or did both sides decide to hold a meeting on their own initiative?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: No we didn't receive any instructions. At the beginning we spoke of as inhabitants of the village of Mrkovici and these other villages on the Muslim side because on the whole, we knew each other. And as neighbours we tried to present incidents from happening, to prevent further incidents from happening after the first one. Unfortunately, this did not succeed because they never respected the agreements.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who participated in those negotiations from your side and from their side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, I can mention some names. May I?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we go into closed session? I wouldn't want certain names to be mentioned which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will turn into closed session -- private session, I should say. Ms. Pilipovic, on the other hand, I don't know whether the testimony until now gives a picture of the situation prior to the time covered by the indictment, and seems to give a similar picture as we have heard several times before. So I wonder how much detail we would need, especially if during that period of time. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, thank you. Mr. DP23, you were the commander of the company, of the Mrkovici company in 1992. Which military formation did your company belong to? Which military formation -- within which military formation did it function in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Our company acted within the Hresa Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who the commander of the Hresa Battalion was, at that time when you were the company commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. Milan Plakalovic was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that there were about 100 men in your company. You tell us what sort of weapons you had. What sort of weapons, light and heavy weapons did the men in your company have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: It might be a problem to explain this in detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead, tell us briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: In April, in Faletici, left of Mrkovici, there was a warehouse, an equipment and weapons warehouse. At the time we found out, we were informed, that the Muslims were approaching from the southern side and they were taking weapons away. So a certain number of Serbs also entered from the north. They also took part of the weapons, some of the weapons. And we received automatic rifles from the battalion and semi-automatic rifles, a 60-millimetre mortar, and three machine-guns, M-53 machine-guns. Those are the weapons that the men in the company had.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, can you tell us what the positions of your company were in September 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, I can describe that to you. But to make this clear to you I have to tell you what happened up until September 1992. Because up until that time, from time to time the lines would move. On the following day, the day after Bajram, the Muslim holiday, we were attacked or rather it was more a matter of provocation; they wanted to see whether we were alert. And on the 6th of April there was a frontal attack launched against us. I think at least 100 men attacked us. At that point in time we were in the first houses in Mrkovici, those are the houses of Milorad Andzic, Mirko Andzic, Redzenovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, when I asked you a question about the positions of your company in September, are you telling us that your company had positions in those houses too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, yes, those are the positions concerned. On the whole, those are the positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP23, can you tell us how long the lines, your Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. company's line was, the front line that your company had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Between 2 and a half and 3 kilometers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, from September 1992 up until August 1994, were you the company commander throughout that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: No. I was the commander up until November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. DP23 are you telling us that from November 1992 you were no longer at that location or did you remain at that location in some other capacity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: From November 1992 as the Army of Republika Srpska and other services had been -- were almost completely organised by that time, I was requested to report to the Ilidza police station where I used to work. So that people were assigned to places where they were able to perform their duties, according to what they were capable of doing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, since in the area of the positions of your company you were there until 1992 and you were the company commander, can you tell us with regard to that period whether you as the company commander received orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, from September up until November while I was there, I did receive orders from the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what sort of orders you received during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: The orders from my commander were that I should inform the men that they shouldn't fire on civilians and civilian property. The orders stated that they had to act in a disciplined matter, and on the whole that's what it boiled down to.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, did you relay those orders to your men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I relayed the orders to my men on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that you did so on several occasions, how often was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Well, officially at least once a week, because a man would be absent and then he would arrive, but sometimes even more frequently.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, as the company commander during that period, did you institute proceedings against one of your men at any given moment, against one of your men who failed to respect your orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: No, I didn't, as this was not necessary. Everything functioned correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, given that you lived in that area, you told us how the lines were established. Can you tell us whether there was any fighting at the front line of your company during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. Fighting occurred on a daily basis. It was very seldom that there was no shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that there was fighting on a daily basis and that not a day passed without fire being opened, can you tell us which positions the BH Army took action from in relation to your company, the position of your company? You tell us whether you know anything about the front lines of the BH Army in relation to the positions of your company? Where were these front lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. The enemy side took action against us from the Grdonj area, from Sedrenik, from the Sedrenik area, from Streliste, from Bakija. It was from those positions. And heavy weapons were -- they had heavy weapons in the depth of their line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, you've mentioned heavy weapons, which were, as you say, in the depths. Do you have personal knowledge of the positions concerned and of the weapons concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I didn't mention this, but from the Kosevo tunnel that goes in the direction of the railway station, there was a Muslim tank which fired --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... perhaps the witness could indicate or could be asked to indicate the source of his information, on what basis he is saying these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, perhaps it would be useful to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, you mentioned that the BH Army was active, took action from the depth from heavy weapons. Can you tell us on the basis of what knowledge are you telling us about the existence of heavy weapons that were active from the depth? Did you see this yourself? Did you personally see this or is this something that you were told by someone, if someone told you about this, tell us who told you about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but shall I first of all answer your question about where they were active from or do you first want to know where I found out about this from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it is the best first to have the basis for the answer laid, Ms. Pilipovic. So would you please first tell us where you got your information from, whether you saw it yourself, whether you heard it, whether -- and then please tell us what the content of your knowledge is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I received information from people, from men on the other side, on the enemy side. I can tell you the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would like these names not to become public, then we will turn into private session. Another day of doing it, Ms. Pilipovic, might be to ask the witness to write down these names during the break so that we do not spend two or three months to --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To write them down, yes, that's what I was thinking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please, during the next break, write down the names of those who gave you information from the opposite side of the lines so that we don't have to discuss spelling, et cetera. If you write them down, we could then use them. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, you told us that you were told of this by certain people whose names you know, and you can tell us their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, can you tell us whether your knowledge of all the positions comes from other people or did you see some of the positions yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I could see some of the positions myself directly, and I obtained information from those people that concerned -- that was of interest for the position where the company was located. Since I was a policeman all information -- it was information that interested us.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that you could see certain positions directly, can you tell us from which position with relation -- in relation to the position of your company were you able to observe the BH Army firing from heavy weapons directly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: To the right of the small fortress, or the so-called Mala Kula. I could directly observe the tunnels from there, the Kosevo stadium, the Ciglana neighbourhood, the Bare town cemetery, and the route towards Kobilja Glava.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, Defence counsel would like to show Mr. DP23 part of the -- part of a map of the town of Sarajevo so that the witness could mark those positions in order for this to be clear to us all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, would you please assist.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document Number D1800.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, could you use a black felt tip to mark and also draw a circle around the positions that you said were the areas of concern. Can you mark the Grdonj area on the map. And can you also mark the Mala Kula area, too.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But could you please move your head a bit so that we can see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: This is Mala Kula. This here below is Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, what can you see, what do you have direct vision of from those positions? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Well, from Mala Kula, you can't see much because down below the area is covered by forest. But to the right, if you look towards the part of the town under Muslim control, our positions were to the right and that is from where you can see what I have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, could you put the map a bit up to the north and can you mark what you could see from those positions, to the west of Mala Kula, as you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. The Ciglana locality -- shall I mark it with a felt tip pen?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You can mark it with a circle and put a "C" in the middle for the neighbourhood that you called Ciglana.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what did you see there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: From the tunnel, on occasions, a tank would come out and fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us in which direction? Did you see this personally and on how many occasions did you see that? How frequent was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, I personally saw it on several occasions. It would fire and then it would go back into the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us in which direction did it fire when you saw it? Were you able to assess that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. It fired mostly on our right flank, which, that was not our unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, you mentioned the cemetery of Bare. Can you tell us from those positions what did you see, from your positions what did you see? Yes, we can see that on the map, but what were you able to observe there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: From that location, the opposing side used mortars, fired with mortars of large calibre, 120-millimetre. On one occasion I think they said they had Howitzers and this is where they were firing on us with artillery. And they were firing on our positions in the depth of the village, but they also fired on us, as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if it is necessary for the transcript, perhaps we don't have to mark it because we can see that the witness is pointing to the city cemetery of Bare that we can see below the word "Sarajevo" in the top part of the map. And the witness tells us that it was from the positions of Mala Kula he was able to observe how large-calibre mortars were fired and how -- and from Howitzers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise it wasn't quite Mala Kula position, it was slightly to the right of Mala Kula.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. DP23, now that you tell us this, bearing in mind the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you ask the witness where he marked what he called Mala Kula, to add an "MK" because it's just one dot on the map at this very moment. Could you please add "MK" to where you marked Mala Kula to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That would then mark Mala Kula.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. DP23, you are telling us west from Mala Kula you were able to observe the firing of the large-calibre mortars and Howitzers firing from the city cemetery. My question was: How frequently did you observe this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I saw that on several occasions. They fired on us several times until we were able to see that. When I spotted them, I informed the higher command. I think that they were neutralised.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, now that you've marked these positions for us of the tunnel, of the Kosevo tunnel, and where the tank and the mortars were active from, is this something that you were able to observe directly from the positions west of Mala Kula?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, that's something that I saw personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Now, as far as the map is concerned, the map that is in front of you, could you mark the locations about which you know that you got information from the people that you will supply the names thereof later on, and who told you about the locations that were used by the BH Army as positions for use by their heavy artillery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. The mortars were still located just below the Kosevo hospital near the engineering faculty. I will try and find my bearings on the map, now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I again -- yes. Could it please be --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, could you please draw a circle around that area and if you can just put "M" there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness marked the location from where mortars were active which is located in the area left from the word "Kosevo" that we can see -- by the Kosevo Hospital that we can see we marked yellow on the map. I don't know whether that is clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, can you mark some other locations on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to avoid confusion, it is on the map right from where it reads "Kosevo" but left from where it reads "Bolnica Kosevo." Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. DP23, on this map can you see other locations, specific locations that you had information about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. I will now try. The information about a mortar that was on a vehicle that was driven from the entrance to Grdonj Mali ^, from Sedrenik, and it moved in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, can you please move your head a little so that we can see what you are marking on the map. And can you tell us where that is, what is the location that you are marking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: This is Sedrenik. Just a moment. And it went this way. It went along this road. So I don't know whether this can be seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, can you tell us if this is a street, a street in Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. This is Sedrenik Street and Balina Kula. And in this direction, the vehicle was driving, or vehicles, on which mortars were mounted. And they were also located -- the mortars were located in the Bare cemetery. Not permanently. This is something that was moved from time to time. In the Bakija cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, before you mark this on this map, can you please indicate the Bakija cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness drew a line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And Witness, could you please mark number "3" next to the word "Sedrenik."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Sedrenik, number 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you just put a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness drew number "3" above the word "Sedrenik." And looking towards west, he drew a line which runs more towards the north. And the witness tells us that this street is the street used by a vehicle which had a mortar mounted on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly, Mr. DP23?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As for the map, you spoke about the Bakija cemetery. So that we can see it, could you please mark this area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In that circle, could you put number "4." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, above the word "Bakija" and the number "4," he marked a location from where mortars were active.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are saying this is Bakija cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, considering that you have marked number 3 and 4, you didn't draw a circle, although you also described it. Could you please draw a circle around the Bare cemetery.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So, perhaps for the record, between the mortars that were located near the Kosevo Hospital, can you draw a number "2" there, can you indicate -- mark number "2" there, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I put an "M" there

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think it would be good to put number "2" there and "M" could mean mortar. Perhaps that would be clearer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you can do a large circle there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has done so already added the "2" to where an "M" is in a larger circle. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, on this map did you mark according to your information and your knowledge, information from other people, you marked the positions from which BH Army fired with heavy weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: The locality of Bakija, I was able to see that occasionally and see it for myself that there was firing going on from that location. And the other locations I would occasionally hear firing but it was impossible to locate it because the terrain is such, the layout of the terrain is such that you could never be absolutely certain where the firing came from. But based on the information given or supplied by the people whose name I will give you later, I found out the locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. DP23.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, considering that Mr. DP23 marked certain locations and told us that this was the area where he was able to observe the firing, the Defence would like to show the witness a photograph, D347, which is a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, there is no objection to showing a photograph, but the introductory comment is leading already. Yes? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If we can try and see how clear this photograph could be. I think that on the video evidence screen, it is clearer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall I start?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, the bottom of the photograph or -- can you tell us where was this photograph taken from, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: This photograph was most probably taken from below the small fort or from the small fort, except that this situation doesn't correspond to the situation that was then at the time when I was there. Now, the wood has been cut down and at that time there was the wood standing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, could you use a pointer to indicate what can be seen from this area that you say this photograph was taken from, from Mala Kula? Can you show us the area that can be seen, or rather which part of the city is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: That is Kosevo stadium. This is Zetra, this is the Ciglana locality, the tunnels. This part here, I was able to see it. But a little further to the right from here. But at that time, from 1992, it wasn't possible from here from where the photograph was taken from because there was wood here. Now, the wood has been cut down so I don't know. Here, to the right, right to the right it is possible to see the view of all of this that has been shot.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, can you tell us in the bottom of the -- or rather in the background of the photograph we can see a hill. Can you tell us what is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: This is Hum hill, if this is what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP23, while you were on these positions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, for the sake of the transcript, the witness pointed at where it appears to be the tower on the hill in the middle of the photograph. Please --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, do you personally know in the period while you were in the area of the Sharpstone, can you tell us which army was on the Hum hill? Do you know, personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: With difficulty. I am sorry. I can only talk to you about Mrkovici or rather the area that I know very well and personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP23, before you had a look at the map and marked the locations that the BH Army fired from heavy weapons, I asked you about the positions of the BH Army in relation to the positions of your company on Sharpstone feature. Can you tell us how far was the front line of the BH Army from you in relation to your positions? So we are talking about the positions on the Sharpstone feature, on Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Well, when there was -- when things were not changing, we were about 100 metres away. And when they were attacking us, it would all get confused, the line would get confused.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that there were moments that a distance was only 100 metres, can you tell us what was the defence line of the BH Army in depth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: The BH Army had three lines of defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what information are you telling us that there were three lines of defence? Is it something that you saw for yourself, that you know personally, or did you hear this from somebody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Some parts it was possible to see by the person from our observation. What we were not able to see for ourselves, it was through these people that we got the information.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say the person from your observation or your observer, can you tell us how many observers did you have and where were they located in the -- along the positions of your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: We had one observation point on the Sharpstone feature, and one to the right of Mala Kula. And for the rest of the line, there was no point because the terrain was wooded, so you couldn't see anything anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly, so you had one observation point near Mala Kula?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: To the right of Mala Kula from which location it is possible to see this part which is on this photograph, the stadium, the city cemetery, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you in the area of the Sharpstone feature, did you have an observation post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, we did. That's what I said. We had an observation post on the Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark in these observation posts in 1992 when you were the company commander, and how did you carry out the observation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: The observation was carried out occasionally because it was particularly on the Sharpstone feature it was very risky, it was an improvised observation post at the time that I was there. It was very risky. And this was done so on occasions, and then the observer would withdraw up to our lines of defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you personally know what the observer was able to see by observing from the Sharpstone feature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. He was able to see Sedrenik, part of Sedrenik not all of it, Grlica Brdo, up to the Bakija cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, bearing in mind the testimony of the witness, the Defence would like to show the map in relation to incident number 3 so that we can all see what the witness is talking about. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document number D1801.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, do you recognise this map, the map which is before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, on this map can you indicate with a pointer what was the area of your company? Let me just tell you that the green line is the VRS line and the light green line is the BH Army line, the positions of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: While, I was there, that is, until November 1992, none of the lines had these positions. These are not correctly marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, can you show us with the pointer what you think, in your opinion --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: This is where the Mala Kula should be.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If you can, perhaps you could mark what the positions of your company were in relation to Sharpstone feature and Mala Kula.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Is it possible to see it?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you could just make it a little thicker with the black pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, on this map could you mark the location for which you say is a location called Velika Kula, the large fort?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. Velika Kula should be around here somewhere, as far as I can find my bearings on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the end of the line that the witness marked going below Mala Kula goes through the circle, through the red circle and it goes up to the north. At the end of that line, the witness marked with a small circle the position of what in his opinion was the position of the large fort, the Velika Kula.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, can you please put the map down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we perhaps -- could you please add first "VK" to where you indicated that Velika Kula was. So near the circle you've drawn.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And perhaps he could be asked to add "MK" for the small fort. I think he pointed to it in the course of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please add "MK" for Mala Kula to -- next to the point where you indicated Mala Kula was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I take it that the map could be removed. Ms. Pilipovic, we are close to -- could you give us an indication on how much time you would still need? I noticed that you used until now, 70 minutes, which is of course considerable less than the two hours you --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think about an hour and 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would bring you over two hours. Or is it --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. No, Your Honour. No. No, Your Honour. I will try -- it will be within two hours. What I said, I have been examining for one hour and 10 minutes, so far so perhaps that was the misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We do agree on that. We will adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, can you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, before we have a look at the map again, D1801, did you write down the names during the break?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the most practical way is that you first look at them, Ms. Pilipovic, and then the Prosecution looks at them, and that we then ask the witness to pronounce them aloud or -- but, then, of course, in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we first then turn into closed session. Private session, I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session again. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, you have written down the names from whom you obtained information about the BH Army positions from which they fired from heavy weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just repeat the positions concerned, the positions that the men whose name you wrote down provided you with information about, which areas were those, in order to be precise? Could you tell us which positions they are and which weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Mobile mortars at the school of civil engineering, very near the Kosevo Hospital, the clinical centre. And then there were forces that would move and would fortify in our direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said information on fortification and on the movement of forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you knew about the positions of the BH Army trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: The first trenches in our direction were about 50 to 100 metres away from us at the edge of the village of Mrkovici. The second trenches were about 50 metres in the depth. And the third ones were in the houses themselves. And I would like to add with regard to the gentleman whose name is the first one on the list I have given you, because of what he did, he was killed later.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling -- is this something that you are telling us because of the information you got?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. He was tortured very badly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have personal knowledge of this or did someone tell you about this and when did this happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. People who were in his neighbourhood told me about this in Grdonj, people who left 20 days after he had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, you've told us about the lines of the trenches. The Defence is now going to show you, as we are dealing with this field, with these issues, and later we shall go back to the map 1801. I will show you map 3765 -- 3756.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic? The transcript says map 3765 -- is it this photograph P3756?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. It is a photograph, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am very familiar with this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, you told us about the lines of the trenches. Can you now tell us where these positions are? Can you see them in this photograph? Can you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: We are talking about our line?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You can first of all tell us where "our line" is. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Just before the small fortress and since the terrain slopes downwards, it goes in front of this house and then to Spicasta Stijena about 20 metres behind the edge of the Sharpstone feature. And then it goes back, it follows an angle of 90 degrees up to the Andzica house it goes to the cross-roads of Barice up to Velika Kula. That's our line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, you mentioned depth of the front line of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the depth concerned is and where the lines are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: The first line, this terrain was covered by a forest at the time up until -- up to this transmitter. This forest has been cut down to an extent now. So they were about 50 metres, between 50 and 80 metres in front of Mala Kula. And then parallel to our positions down this valley towards Spicasta Stijena. Then it went down below Spicasta Stijena to the end and there is a slope here to the right and their line would return towards us, it would run parallel to ours, and it would extend as far as the big fortress or Kula, and they were also about 100 metres from us there. That was their first line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. DP23. You've just marked the first line. Were these positions marked? Do you know about this? Were they marked in any way? How do you know that those were the positions of the first lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Well, it is not difficult to know the position of this first line. When we were attacked, we were able to see where they were attacking us from. And, as I say through intelligence gathered, I don't know whether it would be of interest to point this out, but these two men lived here. One of them lived below the transmitter and the second person lived here. I don't know if you can see it. They had a house here. They are neighbours that I knew very well. I had known them all my life. So I was fully informed about their trenches, about where they had dug in and about the fortifications.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, can you tell us when you first received information about the trenches and about digging in in the area that you have just indicated to us, the BH Army area? What period does this concern? You said that you were there from September to November 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, they --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before the witness proceeds to answer that question, could I ask that, maybe for the record, we could describe where he indicated the persons he referred to lived at. Maybe as simple as how was that at the bottom of the Grdonj --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you would please point again to the house where one of your informers were living, so we can describe that for the transcript. Could you please point at it again. You said the house was somewhere below.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Person number one: Below the transmitter in the first few houses in the photograph. Perhaps these ones that I am pointing to or perhaps to the left, these two houses to the left here. And person number two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the first one. The witness points at what seems to be a horizontal path approximately on the middle of the hill without trees on the left side of the photograph that appear two or three small houses, and as indicated that either in these houses or left from them invisible on the picture his first informer would live. Yes, and the second one who might be still alive? Perhaps we should do that in closed session, Ms. Pilipovic? Would that not be proper? Unless you say there is no problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Closed session. Private session, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into open session now.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown D1801, the map which includes incidents number 3 and 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, before the break you marked the positions of your company for the period during which you were the company commander. Can you tell us whether there was any fighting between the two opposing sides in this area from the positions of your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. Well, while I was there, there was fighting that occurred on an almost daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I show you the places that have been marked with red dots on this map to the right of the map where we have number "8" and in the direction of number "3," you see those two dots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I ask you whether you can see these places, these locations that have been marked from your positions, what can you tell us about that? Could you please lower the map a bit and answer the question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Well, if there was no military activity, then perhaps it would be possible. I can't locate it precisely because since the layout of the terrain is such, it is difficult. If there was no military activity, it would be possible to see them, but when there is military activity, it was impossible from our positions. It was only possible to see it from Spicasta Stijena, but at the time it was impossible to remain at the observation post, and as a result, it was impossible to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned fighting and the positions of the BH Army front line, while fighting was ongoing can you tell us what the direction of fire was, if we are talking about the positions of your company? Could you use the pointer to demonstrate this on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What side and in which direction was fire opened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: When there was fighting. Throughout the entire line they would fire at us --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you use the pointer to show us in relation to the position of your company, what direction was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: They fired at us in this direction, like this. They could do so here, but at Spicasta Stijena they weren't able to do so unless they came out. There was only fighting at Spicasta Stijena if they were there directly. Since we were behind the rock, when we would go out they could shoot here, since we were 15 to 20 metres behind the rock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the opposite party shooting at the position of the witness, or was your question about how fire came from the positions of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my question was about opening of fire from both sides during combat, during fighting. In which direction in relation to the positions of the company of the VRS, that is of your company, when -- where was the fire coming from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you are asking about incoming fire and outgoing fire?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you start with the -- as the witness already did -- with the incoming fire. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, can you please mark from which positions fire was coming from in relation to the positions of your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Firing came on the positions of our company mostly from infantry weapons from their first line, and from heavier weapons, as I told you, where the heavy weapons were located, from those locations, while the infantry fire came directly from their first lines. They were firing on to us and so we were firing on to them. That was exchange of fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP23, I think the only thing we haven't clarified is whether did you have any information about the second and the third line of the BH Army, where were they located and would you be able to indicate them on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I will try, although it was easier for me to do so on the photograph, but I will try. The third line was in the first row of houses. The third line in the houses that we can see on here, and that we were able to see on the previous photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, with a black liner can you please mark the third line on this map, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I am not sure whether these are the first houses. As I said, on the photograph it would have been easier, but if these are the first houses -- no, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, if the witness says that it is easier for him to identify it on the photograph, would it not be wiser to ask him to --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I was just thinking of that. Yes, Your Honour, that's exactly what I was thinking. I would show -- show the witness photographs 3760 and 3758. These are the two photographs that can be joined. Perhaps that would be easier for the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is now completely clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, on this photograph can you please mark what were the third line and the second line, from which BH Army was active? You say from which they were firing with infantry weapons --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I can now show the second line. The second line mostly ran below this road.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, so that we can have it very precise, can you tell us if there are any specific locations that marked that second line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: The second line ran directly below the road next to this house with the white roof on, next to the road. Because there is a road, a macadam road, not for the vehicles, it is like a pedestrian path going to Mrkovici and Barice, and it goes up to this house with the white roof. It just goes below the road. And then mostly from that road goes a second line, and then it climbs parallel with the Sharpstone -- Sharpstone --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And the third line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: The third line was in the houses here, as you can see these group of houses. And over there, below that aerial, below the transmitter, that's where the third line went, in those houses, through the communicating trenches, they were connected. The second, the first line and all this was fully fortified.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, I don't think that you answered my question. When was it that you personally found out that these lines were established together with the communication trenches? When did you find that out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before the witness answers this question, just for the sake of this transcript, we have to identify what he pointed at. When he was talking about the second line, he pointed at a road of which a part can be seen on the foot of the wooded hill in the front of the photograph. And then continued to the left approximately where some cattle seems to be in the meadow just in front of the white -- of the house with the white roof. When he was talking about the third line, he pointed at the group of houses of which one appears in P3760 and the other ones, including the house with the whitish roof on P3758, a group of approximately 15 houses. Please proceed. Now, the next question was, I think, how you -- when you personally found out when these lines were established, together with the communication trenches.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember exactly, but that was well before September of 1992. I think by the end of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, can you tell us whether you in your company when you were the company commander, did you have snipers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you had infantry weapons, three machine-guns, and I believe you said you had a 60-millimetre mortar; did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the area of your company were there mortars and/or artillery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: In the area of our company and throughout the area of Mrkovici there was no artillery.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any information or knowledge whether as part of your battalion, were there any mortars or artillery there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, I do know. There was artillery in the wider area of Hresa, but I am not sure whether that area belonged the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, did you, as a company commander, were you in a situation to ask for the assistance from the battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, that did happen. When there were a larger-scale attacks, we asked for the assistance from the battalion and they would then assess the situation, depending on how it looked. I think that artillery was active from that area, more or less, the wider area of Hresa and we had a unit coming to assist us when we needed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP23, you told us until November 1992 you were the company commander and that after that you went to the area of Ilidza, if I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, I went because there was not enough staff, not enough personnel, I went to the border crossing police station, Ilidza Kobiljaca.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, can you tell us what was your duty in the area of the border crossing post Kobiljaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: At the border crossing post of Kobiljaca we carried out checks, controls, of the persons who were leaving and coming in and all other convoys in accordance with the mandate that we had, including checking the UNHCR, UNPROFOR convoys. And we also had other police tasks to carry out.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, while you were carrying out these duties on the Kobiljaca border post, you said this was the area of Ilidza. Did you then at that time live in Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you personally have knowledge about November -- the period from November 1992 until August 1994, in that area was there fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. There were -- there was fighting, combat activities, and in a position to Mrkovici where there was more infantry fire, the actual area of Ilidza and the centre village where I went to Kobiljaca to work, very frequently, even the very centre of Ilidza was shelled by the opposing side. They were shelled from Mount Igman and Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP23, when you tell us about the locations that the Ilidza area was shelled from, do you personally know where were the positions of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I don't know for certain. I know approximately Mount Igman area, Hrasnica, Otes, Butmir. I know the actual centre of Ilidza was at risk right up to the Blazuj location where our hospital for the wounded was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And another question: When you told us how at the border crossing post at Kobiljaca you were checking the passing of convoys of humanitarian help, when you were there how much time did you spend, say, in a week at this border post checking and controlling the convoys coming in and out come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: On average, 8 to 10 hours daily.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us in your opinion how many convoys went in, how many -- how frequent were the entries of the humanitarian convoys were in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Of the UNHCR and other humanitarian convoys went in on a daily basis. That was the cause of the major traffic jam at the border crossing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any information or knowledge in which direction they were going to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, they were going from the direction of Kiseljak to the part of Sarajevo under Muslim control.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. You will now be examined by counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May it please you, Mr. President. Can we start by going into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is confirmed on my screen now. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: While you were at the area of the Sharpstone feature, the area that your company had responsibility for, you had three M-53 machine-guns; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Those guns are mounted on tripods; is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: No. We had three machine-guns M-53 without tripods.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are those guns the ones which sometimes are called "Death Sowers"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I don't know that they were called that. It is a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the effective range for those guns was up to 1.000 metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were those guns made or manufactured to be used while mounted on a tripod, is that the conventional use of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: No, machine-gun M-53 can be used with a tripod and without a tripod. We didn't receive a tripod, so we used it without one.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. What type of automatic rifle did you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: We had automatic rifles, Kalashnikovs. That was Zastava make.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And what was the effective range of that gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Well, you could fire 300, 400 metres. The range is probably longer than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said or let me ask you: Is it your evidence that there were artillery positions in Hresa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: At Hresa itself, no, because from the large fort it was possible to see the entire Hresa so you would see it. I didn't personally see it. But I know from others that it was in the wider area of Hresa, perhaps in Crepovsko.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were there artillery positions in Hresa attached to any battalion in that area or were they directly attached to the corps headquarters, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I think they were attached to battalion, because when our lines were at risk, I would call the battalion commander, and then the artillery would fire. So I presumed that they were linked or attached to the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What was the name of your battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Milan Plakalovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And what was your rank while your were in the Mrkovici area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I didn't have a rank.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did your battalion have any supporting mortar units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes. In the battalion there was a platoon that had mortars.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How many mortars did this platoon have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I don't know. They were also located outside the territory of Mrkovici and our area of responsibility. I know that they existed. The battalion commander told me so, and they probably assisted us.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Please just answer what I ask. You don't know how many mortars they had, that's your answer. Do you know what type of mortars they had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Why, may I ask, do you say that the supporting fire came from the Hresa area? How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I know the battalion command was located at Hresa, and from the command we requested and occasionally you would be able to hear the firing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in the -- up until you left that region, did you hear mortars being fired from anywhere in the area of Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: No. I know Mrkovici very well because I was born there and it wasn't there, not from the area of Mrkovici, while I was there, while I was in Mrkovici. For later on, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you never heard mortars being fired or artillery weapons being fired from Mrkovici while you were there; is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What was the name of the unit the brigade which was to the right of your brigade as you face Sarajevo, what was that called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I think it was called the Kosevo Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether that brigade had artillery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I don't know. I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Now, looking cross the city to Trebevic, do you know if there were artillery guns and tanks that fired from VRS-controlled areas into the city from Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: I don't know that and I never saw that, personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us about hearing about certain mortar positions. Are you saying that you never heard that there were tanks controlled by the VRS which fired from Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP23
utterances.text: Trebevic is completely the opposite side, so personally I didn't see them. I can't say for sure that there were or there weren't any.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Apart from Hresa do you know where VRS artillery positions encircling the city were located?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour -- Your Honour, my assistant tells me that line 11 -- 1158, the answer of the witness in the answer it says that he was able to see them. Could we please clarify. That is page 53, line 11 -- line 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem is that my --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a problem in interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, my paging is not correct. So the reference would not be -- if you would please ask the witness to repeat the answer and your question because I have some difficulties in finding it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
